headline: KSE-100 slips 0.20% to 170,425.62 as Hormuz tension pushes oil higher; Wall Street retreats, 10-year Treasury tops 5.21% and gold/silver sink over 3% on hawkish Fed bets
mood: Risk-off deepens · Hormuz tension and a hawkish Fed the dual overhang

five_things.html: The KSE-100 opened the week firmer — up as much as 273.36 points to 171,038.58 by mid-morning — before profit-taking and renewed Middle East jitters dragged it to an intraday low of 170,120.50 and a close of 170,425.62, down 339.60 points (−0.20%). Volume eased to 421.01 million shares (from 482.76 million) on traded value of Rs17.74 billion (from Rs19.28 billion), with decliners outnumbering advancers 267 to 181 (48 unchanged) across 496 names. Selling was broad-based across automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs, with index heavyweights HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PPL, PSO and HBL all trading in the red as the oil-driven inflation scare offset earlier optimism around the IMF's fourth EFF review. Business Recorder and The Express Tribune confirm the print.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Opens the Week Lower
five_things.html: US equities fell broadly on Monday as resurgent US-Iran tensions lifted oil and Treasury yields jumped into a data-heavy week: the S&P 500 dropped 0.77% to 7,683.69, the Dow fell 347 points (−0.70%) to 51,481.51, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.92% to 26,820.38. Yahoo Finance and TheStreet confirm the closes.
five_things.sentiment: broadly weaker to start the week

five_things.chip: 10-Year Yield Extends to a Fresh 19-Year High
five_things.html: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to roughly 5.21% on Monday, its highest since 2007, while the 2-year climbed to about 4.94%, its richest level since May 2024, as hawkish commentary from New York Fed President John Williams and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson kept markets pricing close to a 70% chance of another quarter-point hike at the 28 October FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh. The move came alongside a record-weak final University of Michigan sentiment reading of 48.1 and one-year inflation expectations of 4.6%. Babypips and CNBC confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Oil Rebounds as Trump Rejects Iran's Hormuz Offer
five_things.html: Brent settled Monday at $105.28 (after trading as high as $108.83) and WTI at $92.60 (intraday high $96.54), both climbing roughly 2-3% on the session after President Trump confirmed he had rejected Tehran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, reviving the Middle East risk premium just as OPEC+'s seven core members agreed on 6 September to hold October output at September levels. CNBC and Trading Economics confirm.

five_things.chip: Gold and Silver Sink Over 3% as Yields Bite
five_things.html: Gold slid 3.19% to $4,148.69 and silver dropped 4.31% to $61.53 on Monday — a seven-week low for gold — as the fresh oil-driven inflation scare hardened Fed rate-hike bets and lifted Treasury yields, overwhelming any safe-haven bid from Middle East tension. USAGOLD and Kitco confirm the closes.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape opened the week constructively before fading: the KSE-100 shed 0.20% to 170,425.62 as selling in autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs offset an early rally, with breadth turning negative (267 decliners vs 181 advancers). The macro backdrop stays cautiously supportive — the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third consecutive meeting on 14 September, even as CPI inflation returned to double digits at 11.1% YoY in August (from 9.2% in July), per Business Recorder and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. The IMF has begun its fourth EFF review and third RSF review, with roughly $1.1bn (SDR 760m plus SDR 153.8m) riding on the government meeting six of seven quantitative targets and finalising the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill now before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance.
matrix.gcc_html: GCC markets remain anchored by a firmer oil tape and a resilient non-oil economy: Brent's rebound toward $105 on renewed Hormuz risk follows OPEC+'s 6 September decision by its seven core members to hold October output at September levels, having already unwound the 1.65mn bpd voluntary-cut tranche (a further 2mn bpd 2022-vintage cut stays in place through year-end), per EnergyConnects. Non-oil momentum stayed solid into August, with Saudi Arabia's PMI at 53.8 (a six-month high) and the UAE's at 55.3 — its fastest pace since late 2024 — per Arab News and Gulf Today. Saudi's PIF kept up its Vision 2030 deployment pace through September, launching the Tawrid supply-chain financing platform, unveiling CEER's flagship vehicles, and standing up the Gulf Coast Development Company in Al-Khafji, per PIF.
matrix.global_html: Global markets opened the week on the back foot: US equities fell broadly (S&P −0.77%, Nasdaq −0.92%, Dow −0.70%) as the 10-year Treasury yield hit a fresh 19-year high near 5.21% and the 2-year touched 4.94%, with markets pricing roughly 70% odds of another Fed hike on 28 October under Chair Kevin Warsh amid a record-weak University of Michigan sentiment print of 48.1. Fiscal risk was defused for now — President Trump signed a stopgap funding bill on 2 September that funds the government through 11 December, averting the shutdown that would otherwise have begun 1 October, per Breaking Defense — but the underlying driver of Monday's selloff was oil: Brent's jump toward $105 after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal revived inflation fears just as the Fed leans hawkish.

legislative.policy_html: Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — tabled in the Senate, referred to the Standing Committee on Finance & Revenue; tightens SOE governance, disclosure and competitive-procurement rules ahead of the IMF's 4th EFF/3rd RSF review
legislative.sectors: Sovereign Wealth Fund, state-owned banks & enterprises
legislative.impact_html: Wins: governance/transparency advocates, IMF programme credibility, eventual $1.1bn tranche unlock. Loses: officials losing discretionary control over SOE asset transfers; ministries facing tighter oversight.

legislative.policy_html: 15% Pillar Two Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax rollout across all six GCC states, alongside UAE Cabinet Decision No. 17 of 2026 amending tax-procedure executive regulations (effective 1 April 2026)
legislative.sectors: Large multinationals, free-zone entities, holding companies
legislative.impact_html: Wins: GCC treasuries (broader, OECD-aligned tax base; reduced reputational risk of being a low-tax jurisdiction). Loses: in-scope multinational groups with GCC hubs face higher effective tax rates and heavier compliance costs.

legislative.policy_html: Stopgap funding bill signed 2 September funds the federal government through 11 December 2026, averting the 1 October shutdown; Fed under Chair Kevin Warsh signals continued tightening bias into the 28 October FOMC
legislative.sectors: Federal contractors & agencies, rate-sensitive equities, Treasuries
legislative.impact_html: Wins: federal contractors and agencies gain near-term funding certainty. Loses: duration-sensitive and growth equities face another likely hike; the fiscal cliff is deferred to December, not resolved.

levels.support_note: just below Monday's intraday low of 170,120.50; deeper support at 168,000
levels.resistance_note: Monday's intraday high of 171,126.52; then the week's earlier high near 171,159.73

desk_stance_html: The desk reads Monday's action as a risk-off pivot driven by oil and rates, not a local growth story — the KSE-100's 0.20% dip came on broad but orderly selling, with SBP's steady 11.5% policy rate and progress on the IMF's fourth EFF review still net-supportive of the local bull case. The bigger swing factor into Tuesday is external: a Hormuz-driven oil spike toward $105 Brent, a fresh 19-year high in the 10-year Treasury near 5.21%, and a hawkish Fed under Chair Warsh are compressing risk appetite globally, and gold/silver's sharp 3-4% slide shows even safe havens aren't immune to a rate shock. We'd watch 169,500 as first support (deeper at 168,000) and 171,150 as the level to reclaim before calling the pullback over, with 170,425 as the pivot. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 slips as Hormuz tension flares and the Fed stays hawkish — Economic Vibes, 29 September 2026

Monday's tape was a reminder that the biggest swing factor for Pakistani markets right now isn't local — it's oil and US rates.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
The KSE-100 opened the week up as much as 273 points before fading to close at 170,425.62, down 339.60 points (−0.20%), as selling in autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs offset the early rally. Breadth turned negative (267 decliners vs 181 advancers) on volume of 421.01m shares and Rs17.74bn traded value.

Wall Street opened lower too: S&P 500 −0.77% to 7,683.69, Dow −0.70% to 51,481.51, Nasdaq −0.92% to 26,820.38, as the 10-year Treasury yield hit a fresh 19-year high near 5.21% and the 2-year touched 4.94%. Gold and silver each fell over 3% — even havens aren't immune to a rate shock.

PAKISTAN
SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting even as CPI inflation returned to double digits at 11.1% YoY in August. The IMF has begun its fourth EFF review and third RSF review, with roughly $1.1bn riding on the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill now before the Senate.

GCC
OPEC+'s core members held October output at September levels after unwinding the 1.65mn bpd voluntary cut tranche. Non-oil PMIs stayed strong into August (Saudi 53.8, UAE 55.3), and PIF kept deploying Vision 2030 capital — Tawrid supply-chain financing, CEER's flagship vehicles, and the Gulf Coast Development Company in Al-Khafji.

GLOBAL
A stopgap bill signed 2 September funds the US government through 11 December, averting an October 1 shutdown — but the real story is oil: Brent's jump toward $105 after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal revived inflation fears just as the Fed, under Chair Kevin Warsh, leans toward another hike on 28 October.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
🇵🇰 Pakistan: SWF Amendment Bill — wins: governance/IMF credibility; loses: discretionary control over SOE assets.
🌍 GCC: 15% Pillar Two top-up tax — wins: GCC treasuries; loses: in-scope multinationals.
🇺🇸 Global: US funding stopgap to 11 Dec — wins: federal contractors; loses: duration-sensitive equities facing another Fed hike.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support at 169,500 (deeper at 168,000), pivot at 170,425, resistance at 171,150. The desk reads Monday's dip as risk-off driven by oil and rates, not a local growth story — but a hawkish Fed and a Hormuz-driven oil spike are the levels to watch. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
